 (This is the printed contradiction argument “we conclude from (1), (2) that Hⁿ_δ(B) = 0, hence Hⁿ(B) = 0”, with two corrections: the printed bound (1) is stated only for ρ < δ/2 but is used at radius 2ρ_j = diam C_j < δ, so here the density bound is recorded for all ρ < δ via the definition of B_j and the lemma 5.1 for sets of diameter < δ; and the passage to Hⁿ uses all scales δ' ≤ δ. The step marked “XXX” in the source is thereby completed.)
 5.4 Hence {x ∈ A : Θ_∞(x) < 2^{−n}} is Hⁿ-null, i.e. 2^{−n} ≤ Θ^{*n}(Hⁿ_∞, A, x) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ A. In Lean, 2^{−n} is `(2 : ℝ≥0∞) ^ (-n)`, Hⁿ_∞ is `simonHausdorffContentOuter n ∞`, and the hypothesis is `simonHausdorffContent n (ENNReal.ofReal δ) A < ∞` for every real δ > 0. ∎

subproblems.title: Riesz representation for non-negative functionals (Simon 4.12, with 4.1–4.5, 4.8)
subproblems.statement: For every locally compact Hausdorff space X and every additive, positively homogeneous Λ : C_c(X, [0, ∞)) → [0, ∞) (an ℝ≥0-linear map C_c(X, ℝ≥0) → ℝ≥0), there is a Radon outer measure μ on X (Borel regular, finite on compacts, outer regular, inner regular by compacts on open sets) with Λ(f) = ∫_X f dμ for all f.
subproblems.natural_proof:
PROOF OF `RieszPositive` (Simon, Ch. 1, Lemmas 4.1–4.5, 4.8, Remarks 4.13 and Theorem 4.12; printed proofs, transcribed and completed).

Statement. Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space (Lean: `T2Space X`, `LocallyCompactSpace X`; for Hausdorff spaces this is equivalent to Simon's definition that every point has a neighbourhood with compact closure). Let K₊ := C_c(X, [0, ∞)) be the cone of continuous f ≥ 0 with compact support spt f, and Λ : K₊ → [0, ∞) additive and positively homogeneous (Lean: an ℝ≥0-linear map C_c(X, ℝ≥0) → ℝ≥0). Then there is a Radon outer measure μ on X (Def. 4.6: (R1) μ is Borel regular and μ(K) < ∞ for compact K; (R2) μ(A) = inf{μ(U) : U ⊇ A open} for all A; (R3) μ(U) = sup{μ(K) : K ⊆ U compact} for open U) such that Λ(f) = ∫_X f dμ for all f ∈ K₊ (integral with respect to μ on the σ-algebra of μ-measurable sets; Lean `caratheodoryMeasure μ`).

Standard facts: compact subsets of a Hausdorff space are closed; a closed subset of a compact set is compact; Urysohn's lemma for normal spaces; Carathéodory's Lemma 1.6 (μ-measurable sets form a σ-algebra on which μ is countably additive) and Remark 1.3 (A is μ-measurable iff μ(Y) ≥ μ(Y ∖ A) + μ(Y ∩ A) whenever μ(Y) < ∞).

TOPOLOGICAL LEMMAS.
T1 (4.1, 4.2). If K₁, …, K_N ⊆ X are pairwise disjoint compact sets, there are pairwise disjoint open U_j ⊇ K_j. [Printed: for x ∉ K compact, for each y ∈ K pick disjoint open U_y ∋ x, V_y ∋ y; finitely many V_{y_i} cover K and ⋂U_{y_i}, ⋃V_{y_i} separate x and K. For L compact disjoint from K, repeat for x ∈ L and use compactness of L to get disjoint open sets containing L and K. For N sets: for i ≠ j choose disjoint open O_{ij} ⊇ K_i, O_{ji} ⊇ K_j and put U_i := ⋂_{j≠i} O_{ij}; then U_i ∩ U_j ⊆ O_{ij} ∩ O_{ji} = ∅.] In particular a compact Hausdorff space is normal (4.2).
T2 (4.3). If V is a neighbourhood of x, there is an open U_x ∋ x with closure Ū_x compact and Ū_x ⊆ V. [Printed: WLOG V open; take an open W₀ ∋ x with W̄₀ compact and W := W₀ ∩ V. W̄ is compact, hence normal (T1); W̄ ∖ W and {x} are disjoint closed subsets of W̄, so there are open U₁ ∋ x, U₂ ⊇ W̄ ∖ W in X with U₁ ∩ U₂ ∩ W̄ = ∅. Put U_x := U₁ ∩ W. Then U_x ⊆ W̄ ∖ U₂, a closed set contained in W ⊆ V; hence Ū_x ⊆ W̄ ∖ U₂ ⊆ V, and Ū_x is compact as a closed subset of W̄.]
T3 (4.4, Urysohn). If K ⊆ V with K compact and V open, there are an open U ⊇ K with Ū compact, Ū ⊆ V, and a continuous f : X → [0, 1] with f ≡ 1 on a neighbourhood of K and f ≡ 0 on X ∖ U; in particular f ∈ K₊ and spt f ⊆ Ū ⊆ V. [Printed: by T2 and compactness, K ⊆ U := U_{x_1} ∪ ⋯ ∪ U_{x_N} with Ū = ⋃Ū_{x_i} compact ⊆ V. Ū is normal (T1), so Urysohn's lemma gives continuous f₀ : Ū → [0, 1] with f₀ = 1 on K and f₀ = 0 on Ū ∖ U. Let f₁ := f₀ on Ū and 0 on X ∖ U; this is well defined (f₀ = 0 on Ū ∖ U) and continuous by the pasting lemma for the finite closed cover X = Ū ∪ (X ∖ U). Finally f := 2 min{f₁, 1/2} equals 1 on the open set {f₁ > 1/2} ⊇ K and vanishes off U.]
T4 (4.5, partition of unity). If K is compact and U₁, …, U_N are open with K ⊆ ⋃U_j, there are φ_j ∈ K₊, 0 ≤ φ_j ≤ 1, with spt φ_j a compact subset of U_j, Σ_jφ_j ≤ 1 on X and Σ_jφ_j ≡ 1 on a neighbourhood of K. [Printed: by T2 each x ∈ K has an open U_x with Ū_x compact ⊆ some U_j; finitely many U_{x_1}, …, U_{x_M} cover K; let V_j be the union of those U_{x_i} with Ū_{x_i} ⊆ U_j, so V̄_j is compact ⊆ U_j and the V_j cover K. By T3 choose ψ_j : X → [0, 1] continuous with ψ_j ≡ 1 on V̄_j and ψ_j ≡ 0 off an open W_j with W̄_j compact ⊆ U_j; and choose f₀ : X → [0, 1] with f₀ ≡ 1 on a neighbourhood of ⋃_jV̄_j and f₀ ≡ 0 on the closed set {Σ_jψ_j = 0}, whose complement is an open neighbourhood of the compact set ⋃_jV̄_j. Put ψ₀ := 1 − f₀. Then Σ_{i=0}^Nψ_i > 0 everywhere (where Σ_{j≥1}ψ_j = 0 we have ψ₀ = 1), and φ_j := ψ_j/Σ_{i=0}^Nψ_i (j = 1, …, N) are continuous, spt φ_j ⊆ W̄_j ⊆ U_j, Σ_{j≥1}φ_j ≤ 1, and Σ_{j≥1}φ_j = 1 where f₀ = 1, a neighbourhood of K.]

REMARKS 4.13. (1) If f, g ∈ K₊ and f ≤ g then g − f ∈ K₊ and Λ(g) = Λ(f) + Λ(g − f) ≥ Λ(f). (2) If spt f ⊆ K and g ∈ K₊ with g ≥ 1 on K, then f ≤ (sup f)g, so Λ(f) ≤ (sup f)Λ(g).

CONSTRUCTION. For open U let μ(U) := sup{Λ(f) : f ∈ K₊, f ≤ 1, spt f ⊆ U} (1), and for arbitrary A let μ(A) := inf{μ(U) : U ⊇ A open} (2). The definitions agree on open sets because (1) is monotone in U.

P1 (finiteness on compacts; formula (3)). For compact K:
  (3) μ(K) = inf{Λ(g) : g ∈ K₊, g ≤ 1, g ≡ 1 on a neighbourhood of K} < ∞.
 “≤”: if g ≡ 1 on an open O ⊇ K and g ≤ 1, then every f ∈ K₊ with f ≤ 1 and spt f ⊆ O satisfies f ≤ g (f ≤ 1 = g on O, f = 0 off O), so μ(K) ≤ μ(O) ≤ Λ(g) by Remark 4.13(1). “≥”: for every open U ⊇ K, T3 gives g ∈ K₊ with g ≤ 1, g ≡ 1 near K and spt g ⊆ U, so Λ(g) ≤ μ(U); take the infimum over U. Finiteness: T3 gives such a g at all, so μ(K) ≤ Λ(g) < ∞.

P2 (μ is an outer measure). μ(∅) = 0 (only f = 0 has spt f ⊆ ∅) and μ is monotone. Let U = ⋃_jU_j with U_j open, and f ∈ K₊, f ≤ 1, spt f ⊆ U. By compactness spt f ⊆ U₁ ∪ ⋯ ∪ U_N for some N; T4 gives φ₁, …, φ_N with spt φ_j ⊆ U_j compact and Σφ_j ≡ 1 near spt f. Then f = Σ_jφ_jf with φ_jf ∈ K₊, φ_jf ≤ 1, spt(φ_jf) ⊆ U_j, so Λ(f) = Σ_jΛ(φ_jf) ≤ Σ_jμ(U_j). Taking the supremum over f, μ(U) ≤ Σ_jμ(U_j). For arbitrary A_j and ε > 0 choose open U_j ⊇ A_j with μ(U_j) ≤ μ(A_j) + 2^{−j}ε; then μ(⋃A_j) ≤ μ(⋃U_j) ≤ Σ_jμ(A_j) + ε.

P3 ((R2), (R3)). (R2) holds by definition (2). (R3): if U is open, f ∈ K₊, f ≤ 1, spt f ⊆ U, then by (3) Λ(f) ≤ μ(spt f) (every g ≤ 1 with g ≡ 1 near spt f satisfies f ≤ g); so μ(U) ≤ sup{μ(K) : K ⊆ U compact} ≤ μ(U).

P4 (additivity on disjoint compacts; printed). Let K₁, K₂ be disjoint compact sets and ε > 0. By (3) choose g ∈ K₊, g ≤ 1, g ≡ 1 on a neighbourhood of K₁ ∪ K₂, with Λ(g) ≤ μ(K₁ ∪ K₂) + ε. By T1 choose disjoint open U₁ ⊇ K₁, U₂ ⊇ K₂, and by T3 f_i ∈ K₊ with f_i ≤ 1, f_i ≡ 1 near K_i, spt f_i ⊆ U_i. Then f_ig ∈ K₊, f_ig ≤ 1, f_ig ≡ 1 near K_i, so μ(K_i) ≤ Λ(f_ig) by (3); and f₁ + f₂ ≤ 1 (disjoint supports), so (f₁ + f₂)g ≤ g. Hence μ(K₁) + μ(K₂) ≤ Λ(f₁g) + Λ(f₂g) = Λ((f₁ + f₂)g) ≤ Λ(g) ≤ μ(K₁ ∪ K₂) + ε. With subadditivity, μ(K₁ ∪ K₂) = μ(K₁) + μ(K₂) < ∞.

P5 (Lemma 4.8: μ is a Radon measure). Borel hulls: given A with μ(A) < ∞, (R2) gives open U_k ⊇ A with μ(U_k) < μ(A) + 1/k, so G := ⋂_kU_k is Borel, G ⊇ A, μ(G) = μ(A); if μ(A) = ∞ take G := X. Open sets are μ-measurable (printed): let U be open, Y ⊆ X with μ(Y) < ∞, ε > 0. By (R2) choose open V ⊇ Y with μ(V) < μ(Y) + ε; by (R3) a compact K₁ ⊆ V ∩ U with μ(V ∩ U) ≤ μ(K₁) + ε; and, V ∖ K₁ being open (K₁ is closed), a compact K₂ ⊆ V ∖ K₁ with μ(V ∖ K₁) ≤ μ(K₂) + ε. Since V ∖ U ⊆ V ∖ K₁, using P4 and monotonicity,
  μ(V ∖ U) + μ(V ∩ U) ≤ μ(V ∖ K₁) + μ(K₁) + ε ≤ μ(K₂) + μ(K₁) + 2ε = μ(K₁ ∪ K₂) + 2ε ≤ μ(V) + 2ε ≤ μ(Y) + 3ε,
and μ(Y ∖ U) + μ(Y ∩ U) ≤ μ(V ∖ U) + μ(V ∩ U). As ε is arbitrary, Remark 1.3 shows U is μ-measurable. The μ-measurable sets form a σ-algebra (Lemma 1.6) containing the open sets, hence all Borel sets. With the Borel hulls and P1, (R1) holds; with P3, μ is a Radon measure.

P6 (representation; printed, with the level sets f^{−1}{t_j} accounted for).
 (4) Λ(h) ≤ μ({h > 0})·sup h for h ∈ K₊. Proof: for compact K ⊇ spt h and g ∈ K₊ with g ≤ 1, g ≡ 1 near K, Remark 4.13(2) gives Λ(h) ≤ (sup h)Λ(g); by (3), Λ(h) ≤ (sup h)μ(K). For η > 0 let h_η := max{h − η, 0} ∈ K₊; spt h_η ⊆ {h ≥ η}, a compact subset of {h > 0}, so Λ(h_η) ≤ (sup h)μ({h > 0}). Also 0 ≤ h − h_η = min{h, η} ≤ ηg' for a fixed g' ∈ K₊ with g' ≡ 1 on spt h (T3), so Λ(h) − Λ(h_η) = Λ(h − h_η) ≤ ηΛ(g') → 0 (η ↓ 0).
 Now let f ∈ K₊, K := spt f, ε > 0; if f ≡ 0 both sides vanish. The sets f^{−1}{t}, t > 0, are pairwise disjoint μ-measurable subsets of K and μ(K) < ∞, so μ(f^{−1}{t}) > 0 for at most countably many t. Choose 0 = t₀ < t₁ < ⋯ < t_N with t_{N−1} < sup f < t_N, t_j − t_{j−1} < ε and μ(f^{−1}{t_j}) = 0 for j = 1, …, N. Let U_j := f^{−1}((t_{j−1}, t_j)): open, pairwise disjoint, contained in K.
 By (1) choose g_j ∈ K₊, g_j ≤ 1, spt g_j ⊆ U_j, with Λ(g_j) ≥ μ(U_j) − ε/N. By (R3) and the measurability of compact sets choose a compact K_j ⊆ U_j with μ(U_j ∖ K_j) < ε/N (μ(U_j) < ∞). By T3 choose h_j ∈ K₊, h_j ≤ 1, h_j ≡ 1 near the compact set K_j ∪ spt g_j, spt h_j ⊆ U_j. Then g_j ≤ h_j and
  (5) μ(U_j) − ε/N ≤ Λ(g_j) ≤ Λ(h_j) ≤ μ(U_j).
 The supports of the h_j are disjoint, so Σ_jh_j ≤ 1 and f − fΣ_jh_j ∈ K₊. If f(x)(1 − Σh_j(x)) > 0, then f(x) > 0, and either f(x) = t_j for some 1 ≤ j < N, or x ∈ U_j for the j with f(x) ∈ (t_{j−1}, t_j) and then x ∉ K_j (as h_j = 1 on K_j). So {f − fΣh_j > 0} ⊆ ⋃_j(U_j ∖ K_j) ∪ ⋃_jf^{−1}{t_j}, and (4) gives
  (6) Λ(f − fΣ_jh_j) ≤ (Σ_jμ(U_j ∖ K_j) + 0)·sup f ≤ ε sup f.
 On spt h_j ⊆ U_j we have t_{j−1}h_j ≤ fh_j ≤ t_jh_j, so by linearity, (5) and t_{j−1} ≤ sup f:
  Σ_jt_{j−1}μ(U_j) − ε sup f ≤ Σ_jt_{j−1}Λ(h_j) ≤ Λ(fΣh_j) ≤ Σ_jt_jΛ(h_j) ≤ Σ_jt_jμ(U_j),
 and adding (6): Σ_jt_{j−1}μ(U_j) − ε sup f ≤ Λ(f) ≤ Σ_jt_jμ(U_j) + ε sup f. On the other hand f vanishes off ⋃_jU_j ∪ ⋃_jf^{−1}{t_j}, the latter set being μ-null, and t_{j−1} ≤ f ≤ t_j on U_j, so Σ_jt_{j−1}μ(U_j) ≤ ∫_Xf dμ ≤ Σ_jt_jμ(U_j). Both Λ(f) and ∫_Xf dμ therefore lie in an interval of length Σ_j(t_j − t_{j−1})μ(U_j) + 2ε sup f ≤ ε(μ(K) + 2 sup f). As ε > 0 is arbitrary, Λ(f) = ∫_Xf dμ.

Conclusion. μ is a Radon outer measure (P5) and Λ(f) = ∫_X f dμ for all f ∈ K₊ (P6); the integral of the bounded continuous compactly supported real function f against the measure μ (finite on spt f) is the Lean integral ∫ (f x : ℝ) ∂(caratheodoryMeasure μ). ∎

Formalization note (non-binding): Mathlib's Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem (`MeasureTheory.NNRealRMK.integral_rieszMeasure` and the instance `rieszMeasure_regular`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/RieszMarkovKakutani/NNReal.lean, after equipping X with `borel X`) gives a regular measure ν with ∫ f dν = Λ f; SimonGMT `isRadonOuterMeasure_toOuterMeasure` (Chapter01/RadonOuterMeasure.lean) shows ν.toOuterMeasure satisfies (R1)–(R3), and `integral_radonCaratheodoryMeasure` (Chapter01/RadonCaratheodoryIntegral.lean) or `integral_trim` (the Carathéodory measure trims to ν on Borel sets) identifies the integrals.
proof_key_steps: Topological lemmas 4.1–4.5: separation of disjoint compacts, relatively compact neighbourhoods, Urysohn's lemma, partitions of unity.
Define μ(U) := sup{Λ(f) : f ≤ 1, spt f ⊆ U} for open U and μ(A) := inf{μ(U) : U ⊇ A open}.
Formula (3) for compact sets; μ is an outer measure via partitions of unity; (R2) and (R3) hold.
Additivity on disjoint compacts; Lemma 4.8 then makes open sets measurable and gives Borel hulls, so μ is a Radon measure.
Λ(h) ≤ μ({h > 0})·sup h; a level-set partition with μ-null levels t_j puts Λ(f) and ∫f dμ in one interval of length ≤ ε(μ(spt f) + 2 sup f).

subproblems.title: Riesz representation theorem, vector-valued (Simon 4.14, with 4.7, 4.10)
subproblems.statement: For every locally compact Hausdorff space X, finite-dimensional real inner product space H, and linear L : C_c(X; H) → ℝ that is bounded above on {f : |f| ≤ 1, spt f ⊆ K} for each compact K, there are a Radon outer measure μ on X and a μ-measurable ν : X → H with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. and L(f) = ∫_X ⟨f, ν⟩ dμ for all f ∈ C_c(X; H).
subproblems.natural_proof:
PROOF OF `RieszVector` (Simon, Ch. 1, Lemma 4.7, Theorem 4.10, Theorem 4.14; printed proofs, transcribed and completed; the L¹-duality step is localized to compact sets because a Radon measure on a general locally compact Hausdorff space need not be σ-finite).

Statement. Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space, H a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and L : C_c(X; H) → ℝ linear such that for every compact K ⊆ X the set {L(f) : f ∈ C_c(X; H), |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, spt f ⊆ K} is bounded above. Then there are a Radon outer measure μ on X (Def. 4.6) and a μ-measurable ν : X → H (preimages of Borel sets are μ-measurable) with |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. and L(f) = ∫_X ⟨f, ν⟩ dμ for all f ∈ C_c(X; H) (integrals with respect to μ on the μ-measurable sets; Lean `caratheodoryMeasure μ`).

Dependency. Theorem 4.12 = sibling `riesz_positive` (Lean `Submission.riesz_positive : RieszPositive`).
Standard facts: Lemma 1.6 / Remark 1.7 (Carathéodory); Urysohn's lemma for locally compact Hausdorff spaces (Simon 4.4: for K compact ⊆ V open there is f ∈ C_c(X, [0, 1]) with f ≡ 1 near K and spt f ⊆ V); disjoint compact sets have disjoint open neighbourhoods (Simon 4.1); every compact set has an open neighbourhood with compact closure; simple functions are dense in L¹; for a finite measure space, every bounded linear functional on L¹ is given by a bounded measurable function (L¹–L^∞ duality); Zorn's lemma.

STEP 0 (reductions). Let n := dim H. If n = 0 then H = {0}, C_c(X; H) = {0}, L = 0, and μ := 0 (the zero outer measure, which satisfies (R1)–(R3)) with ν := 0 works: L(f) = 0 = ∫⟨f, ν⟩ dμ, ν is measurable, and “|ν| = 1 μ-a.e.” holds because μ = 0. Assume n ≥ 1. An orthonormal basis e₁, …, e_n of H gives a linear isometry H ≅ ℝⁿ preserving inner products; transporting L, the hypothesis and the conclusion along it, we may assume H = ℝⁿ (printed: “By using an orthonormal basis for H, it suffices to prove the theorem with H = ℝⁿ”). |·| is the Euclidean norm. K₊ := C_c(X, [0, ∞)).

STEP 1 (the positive functional; printed). For f ∈ K₊ let λ(f) := sup{L(ω) : ω ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ), |ω| ≤ f}.
 • 0 ≤ λ(f) < ∞: ω = 0 is admissible; if |ω| ≤ f then spt ω ⊆ spt f =: K, and if s := sup f > 0 then ω/s is admissible in the hypothesis for K, so L(ω) ≤ s·M_K with M_K an upper bound (if s = 0 then ω = 0).
 • λ(cf) = cλ(f) for c ≥ 0 (c = 0: only ω = 0; c > 0: ω ↦ cω is a bijection between the admissible sets).
 • λ(f + g) ≤ λ(f) + λ(g): given ω with |ω| ≤ f + g let ω₁ := fω/(f + g), ω₂ := gω/(f + g) where f + g > 0, and ω₁ = ω₂ := 0 where f + g = 0. Then ω₁ + ω₂ = ω, |ω₁| ≤ f, |ω₂| ≤ g, and ω₁, ω₂ ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ): they are continuous where f + g > 0, and at a point x₀ with f(x₀) + g(x₀) = 0 we have |ω_i(x)| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ f(x) + g(x) → 0 as x → x₀; their supports lie in spt ω. So L(ω) = L(ω₁) + L(ω₂) ≤ λ(f) + λ(g).
 • λ(f + g) ≥ λ(f) + λ(g): if |ω₁| ≤ f and |ω₂| ≤ g then |ω₁ + ω₂| ≤ f + g, so L(ω₁) + L(ω₂) ≤ λ(f + g).
 Thus λ is an ℝ≥0-linear map K₊ → [0, ∞), and Theorem 4.12 (sibling `riesz_positive`) gives a Radon outer measure μ on X with
  (**) sup{L(ω) : |ω| ≤ f} = λ(f) = ∫_X f dμ for all f ∈ K₊.
 Consequently, for ω ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ): |ω| ∈ K₊ and L(ω) ≤ λ(|ω|), L(−ω) ≤ λ(|ω|), i.e.
  (†) |L(ω)| ≤ ∫_X |ω| dμ.

STEP 2 (Lemma 4.7; printed). If A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞ then μ(A) = sup{μ(K) : K ⊆ A compact}. [Given ε > 0 choose open U ⊇ A with μ(U ∖ A) < ε (R2), compact K ⊆ U with μ(U ∖ K) < ε (R3), and open W ⊇ U ∖ A with μ(W) < 2ε (R2). Then K ∖ W is compact, K ∖ W ⊆ U ∖ W ⊆ A, and μ(A ∖ (K ∖ W)) ≤ μ(U ∖ K) + μ(W) < 3ε.]

STEP 3 (Theorem 4.10 for p = 1; printed). C_c(X) is dense in L¹(μ), and hence (componentwise) C_c(X; ℝⁿ) is dense in L¹(μ; ℝⁿ). [Let f ∈ L¹(μ), ε > 0. Choose a simple φ = Σ_{j=1}^N a_j1_{A_j} with distinct a_j ≠ 0 and pairwise disjoint μ-measurable A_j with ‖f − φ‖₁ < ε; then μ(A_j) < ∞. Let M > max|a_j| and η := ε/(2MN). By Step 2 choose compact K_j ⊆ A_j with μ(A_j ∖ K_j) < η and by (R2) open U_j ⊇ K_j with μ(U_j ∖ K_j) < η; replacing U_j by U_j ∩ U'_j with pairwise disjoint open U'_j ⊇ K_j (Simon 4.1), the U_j are pairwise disjoint. By Urysohn choose g_j ∈ C_c(X) with g_j = a_j on K_j, |g_j| ≤ |a_j|, spt g_j ⊆ U_j, and put g := Σ_jg_j. Then g = φ on ⋃K_j, |φ − g| ≤ 2M, and φ − g vanishes off ⋃_j((U_j ∖ K_j) ∪ (A_j ∖ K_j)), so ‖φ − g‖₁ ≤ 2M·Σ_j2η = 2ε and ‖f − g‖₁ < 3ε.]

STEP 4 (extension of L to L¹). Each ω ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ) is μ-integrable (bounded, μ(spt ω) < ∞). By (†), L(ω) depends only on the class of ω in L¹(μ; ℝⁿ) and |L(ω) − L(ω')| ≤ ‖ω − ω'‖₁. By Step 3, L extends uniquely to a linear functional L̄ on L¹(μ; ℝⁿ) with |L̄(F)| ≤ ‖F‖₁ (printed: “L_j(f) := L(fe_j) extends to a bounded linear functional on L¹(μ)”).

STEP 5 (local duality; printed “by the Riesz representation theorem for L¹(μ)”, applied on sets of finite measure). Let E be μ-measurable with μ(E) < ∞. For i = 1, …, n the map h ↦ L̄(1_E h e_i) is a linear functional on L¹(μ⌞E) of norm ≤ 1; since μ⌞E is finite, L¹–L^∞ duality gives a bounded μ-measurable ν_{E,i} (zero off E) with L̄(1_E h e_i) = ∫_E h ν_{E,i} dμ. Put ν_E := (ν_{E,1}, …, ν_{E,n}); then L̄(1_E G) = ∫_E ⟨G, ν_E⟩ dμ for all G ∈ L¹(μ; ℝⁿ).
 • |ν_E| ≤ 1 μ-a.e. on E: for η > 0 let S := {x ∈ E : |ν_E(x)| > 1 + η} and G := 1_S ν_E/|ν_E|; then (1 + η)μ(S) ≤ ∫_S|ν_E| dμ = L̄(1_E G) ≤ ‖G‖₁ = μ(S), so μ(S) = 0.
 • Consistency: if E ⊆ E' both have finite measure, then for bounded measurable G vanishing off E, ∫_E⟨G, ν_E⟩ dμ = L̄(1_E G) = L̄(1_{E'}G) = ∫_E⟨G, ν_{E'}⟩ dμ; with G := 1_E(ν_E − ν_{E'}) this gives ν_E = ν_{E'} μ-a.e. on E. Consequently, for any two compact F, F', ν_F = ν_{F∪F'} = ν_{F'} μ-a.e. on F ∩ F'.

STEP 6 (decomposition of a Radon measure into compact pieces).
 6.1 For compact F let S_F := {x ∈ F : μ(F ∩ O) > 0 for every open O ∋ x} (the support of μ⌞F). S_F is closed (if x ∈ F ∖ S_F, some open O ∋ x has μ(F ∩ O) = 0, and then O ∩ S_F = ∅), hence compact, and μ(F ∖ S_F) = 0: F ∖ S_F is μ-measurable with finite measure, every compact C ⊆ F ∖ S_F is covered by finitely many open O with μ(F ∩ O) = 0, so μ(C) = 0, and Step 2 gives μ(F ∖ S_F) = 0.
 6.2 By Zorn's lemma there is a family 𝓕 of compact sets, maximal among families with μ(F) > 0 for F ∈ 𝓕 and μ(F ∩ F') = 0 for distinct F, F' ∈ 𝓕 (the union of a chain of such families is such a family).
 6.3 For compact K, 𝓕_K := {F ∈ 𝓕 : μ(K ∩ F) > 0} is countable: for distinct F₁, …, F_N ∈ 𝓕 the sets F_i' := F_i ∖ ⋃_{l≠i}F_l are disjoint and μ(F_i ∖ F_i') = 0, so Σ_iμ(K ∩ F_i) = μ(K ∩ ⋃F_i') ≤ μ(K) < ∞; hence at most m·μ(K) members have μ(K ∩ F) > 1/m.
 6.4 For compact K, μ(K ∖ ⋃_{F∈𝓕_K}F) = 0: otherwise K' := K ∖ ⋃_{𝓕_K}F (μ-measurable, a countable union being removed) has 0 < μ(K') < ∞, and Step 2 gives a compact C ⊆ K' with μ(C) > 0; C is disjoint from every F ∈ 𝓕_K and μ(C ∩ F) ≤ μ(K ∩ F) = 0 for F ∈ 𝓕 ∖ 𝓕_K; C ∉ 𝓕 (else C ∈ 𝓕_K, but C ∩ C = C ≠ ∅); so 𝓕 ∪ {C} contradicts maximality.
 6.5 For compact K, 𝓕'_K := {F ∈ 𝓕 : S_F ∩ K ≠ ∅} is countable: choose an open O ⊇ K with Ō compact; if x ∈ S_F ∩ K then μ(F ∩ O) > 0, so μ(F ∩ Ō) > 0 and F ∈ 𝓕_{Ō}, which is countable by 6.3.
 6.6 For F ∈ 𝓕 let P_F := S_F ∖ ⋃_{F'∈𝓕, F'≠F}S_{F'}. The P_F are pairwise disjoint; for compact K, P_F ∩ K = ∅ unless F ∈ 𝓕'_K, and P_F ∩ K = (S_F ∩ K) ∖ ⋃_{F'∈𝓕'_K, F'≠F}S_{F'} is a Borel set (6.5). Moreover μ(K ∖ ⋃_{F∈𝓕'_K}P_F) = 0: a point x ∈ K in no P_F either lies outside ⋃_{F∈𝓕_K}F (a null set by 6.4), or lies in some F ∈ 𝓕_K but not in S_F (a subset of the null set F ∖ S_F, 6.1), or lies in S_F ∩ S_{F'} ⊆ F ∩ F' for some distinct F, F' ∈ 𝓕'_K (then F, F' ∈ 𝓕'_K since x ∈ K, and μ(F ∩ F') = 0); these are countably many null sets.

STEP 7 (gluing the local fields). Define ν : X → ℝⁿ by ν := ν_F on P_F (F ∈ 𝓕) and ν := e₁ on X ∖ ⋃_{F∈𝓕}P_F.
 7.1 (Localization principle.) A set T ⊆ X is μ-measurable if T ∩ K is μ-measurable for every compact K. [Let Y ⊆ X with μ(Y) < ∞ and ε > 0; by (R2) take open U ⊇ Y with μ(U) < ∞, and by (R3) (U is μ-measurable) a compact K ⊆ U with μ(U ∖ K) < ε. Since T ∩ K is μ-measurable, μ(Y ∩ T) + μ(Y ∖ T) ≤ μ(Y ∩ K ∩ T) + μ((Y ∩ K) ∖ T) + 2μ(Y ∖ K) ≤ μ(Y ∩ K) + 2ε ≤ μ(Y) + 2ε; conclude by Remark 1.3.]
 7.2 ν is μ-measurable: for a Borel G ⊆ ℝⁿ and compact K, ν^{−1}(G) ∩ K = ⋃_{F∈𝓕'_K}(ν_F^{−1}(G) ∩ P_F ∩ K) ∪ (either K ∖ ⋃_{F∈𝓕'_K}P_F or ∅, according as e₁ ∈ G or not), a countable union of μ-measurable sets; apply 7.1.
 7.3 For compact K, ν = ν_K μ-a.e. on K: on K ∩ P_F (F ∈ 𝓕'_K), ν = ν_F = ν_K μ-a.e. (Step 5, consistency on K ∩ F), and K ∖ ⋃_{F∈𝓕'_K}P_F is null (6.6). In particular |ν| ≤ 1 μ-a.e. on each compact set.

STEP 8 (representation; printed (*)). For ω ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ) let K := spt ω. Then ω = 1_Kω and, by Steps 4, 5 and 7.3,
  L(ω) = L̄(1_Kω) = ∫_K⟨ω, ν_K⟩ dμ = ∫_K⟨ω, ν⟩ dμ = ∫_X⟨ω, ν⟩ dμ.

STEP 9 (|ν| = 1 locally a.e.; printed argument). Let f ∈ K₊ and K := spt f.
 (i) For ω with |ω| ≤ f, Cauchy–Schwarz gives L(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ν⟩ dμ ≤ ∫ f|ν| dμ; by (**), ∫f dμ ≤ ∫f|ν| dμ.
 (ii) Let ν̂ := ν/|ν| where ν ≠ 0 and ν̂ := 0 elsewhere. 1_Kν̂ ∈ L¹(μ; ℝⁿ), so by Step 3 there are g_k ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ) with ∫|g_k − 1_Kν̂| dμ → 0. Let R be the nearest-point retraction of ℝⁿ onto the closed unit ball (R(y) = y for |y| ≤ 1, y/|y| otherwise); it is continuous, R(0) = 0, and |R(y) − v| ≤ |y − v| whenever |v| ≤ 1. So ĝ_k := R ∘ g_k ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ), |fĝ_k| ≤ f, and |ĝ_k − ν̂| ≤ |g_k − ν̂| on K. Hence, using |ν| ≤ 1 a.e. on K,
  |L(fĝ_k) − ∫f|ν| dμ| = |∫_K f⟨ĝ_k − ν̂, ν⟩ dμ| ≤ (sup f)∫|g_k − 1_Kν̂| dμ → 0,
 and L(fĝ_k) ≤ λ(f) = ∫f dμ by (**). So ∫f|ν| dμ ≤ ∫f dμ.
 Thus ∫f(1 − |ν|) dμ = 0 for every f ∈ K₊, with f(1 − |ν|) ≥ 0 a.e. For compact K choose (Urysohn) f ∈ K₊ with f ≡ 1 on K; then 1 − |ν| = 0 μ-a.e. on K. So |ν| = 1 μ-a.e. on every compact set.

STEP 10 (a field of norm exactly one). Let ν' := ν on {|ν| = 1} and ν' := e₁ on {|ν| ≠ 1}. Then ν' is μ-measurable ({|ν| = 1} is μ-measurable by 7.2), |ν'(x)| = 1 for every x ∈ X — so in particular |ν'| = 1 μ-a.e., i.e. μ({|ν'| ≠ 1}) = μ(∅) = 0 — and ν' = ν μ-a.e. on each compact set (Step 9), so Step 8 gives L(ω) = ∫_{spt ω}⟨ω, ν'⟩ dμ = ∫_X⟨ω, ν'⟩ dμ for all ω ∈ C_c(X; ℝⁿ). (Replacing ν by ν' avoids asserting that a set which is null on every compact set is globally null, which may fail for non-σ-finite Radon measures.)

Conclusion. μ (Step 1) is a Radon outer measure and ν' : X → ℝⁿ ≅ H is μ-measurable with |ν'| = 1 μ-a.e. and L(f) = ∫_X⟨f, ν'⟩ dμ for every f ∈ C_c(X; H). ∎

proof_key_steps: Reduce to H = ℝⁿ by an orthonormal basis; n = 0 is handled by μ = 0.
λ(f) := sup{L(ω) : |ω| ≤ f} is additive and positively homogeneous; Theorem 4.12 gives a Radon μ with λ(f) = ∫f dμ, hence |L(ω)| ≤ ∫|ω| dμ.
Lemma 4.7 and Theorem 4.10 (C_c dense in L¹); extend L to L̄ on L¹(μ; ℝⁿ) with norm ≤ 1.
Local L¹–L^∞ duality on each set of finite measure gives consistent fields ν_E with |ν_E| ≤ 1.
A maximal almost-disjoint family of compacts, with supports S_F and cores P_F, glues the ν_F into one ν, measurable by the compact localization principle.
Representation L(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ν⟩ dμ; |ν| = 1 locally a.e. via Cauchy–Schwarz and approximants composed with the radial retraction.
Replace non-unit values by e₁: |ν'| = 1 everywhere, with the same representation and measurability.

subproblems.title: Compactness theorem for Radon measures, corrected (Simon 4.16 with erratum)
subproblems.statement: For every second countable locally compact Hausdorff space X and every sequence of Radon outer measures μ_k on X with sup_k μ_k(K) < ∞ for each compact K, there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a Radon outer measure μ on X with ∫ f dμ_{φ(k)} → ∫ f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : X → ℝ.
subproblems.natural_proof:
PROOF OF `RadonCompactness` (Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 4.16, corrected as in the chapter README erratum; printed proof with the documented correction).

Statement (corrected 4.16). Let X be a locally compact Hausdorff space which is second countable, and let (μ_k)_{k∈ℕ} be Radon outer measures on X (Def. 4.6) with sup_k μ_k(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ X. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a Radon outer measure μ on X with lim_{k→∞} ∫_X f dμ_{φ(k)} = ∫_X f dμ for every continuous f : X → ℝ with compact support (integrals with respect to the measures on the μ_k- resp. μ-measurable sets; Lean `caratheodoryMeasure`).

Erratum being applied. As printed (X only locally compact, σ-compact, Hausdorff) the theorem is false: the Alaoglu step yields a convergent subnet, not a subsequence (counterexample: Dirac masses on the compact cube {0,1}^{𝒫(ℕ)}; SimonGMT `simon_theorem_4_16_counterexample`). The correction adds second countability (equivalently: X is a locally compact separable metrizable space, the standing assumption announced for §4). With it each C(K_j) below is separable, and the Alaoglu step is replaced by its sequential version, proved directly by a diagonal argument (Step 4). We also choose the exhaustion with K_j ⊆ int K_{j+1}, which the printed sentence “F(f) = F_j(f|K_j) whenever spt f ⊆ K_j” needs in order to define F on every f ∈ C_c(X).

Dependency. Theorem 4.12 = sibling `riesz_positive` (Lean `Submission.riesz_positive : RieszPositive`).
Standard facts: a locally compact Hausdorff space is regular; a second countable regular space is metrizable (Urysohn); subspaces of second countable spaces are second countable; C(K) (real continuous functions with the sup norm) is separable for compact metrizable K; Bolzano–Weierstrass for bounded real sequences; Lemma 1.6/Remark 1.7.

STEP 1 (topology). X is σ-compact: every point has an open neighbourhood with compact closure, and a countable base contains countably many such relatively compact basic sets covering X. Write X = ⋃_m C_m with C_m compact. Define compact sets K₁ := C₁ and K_{j+1} := a compact set whose interior contains K_j ∪ C_{j+1} (cover the compact set K_j ∪ C_{j+1} by finitely many open sets with compact closures and take the union of the closures). Then K_j ⊆ int K_{j+1}, ⋃_jK_j = X, and every compact C ⊆ X lies in some K_j (the increasing open sets int K_{j+1} cover C). Each K_j is a compact metrizable space (X is metrizable), so C(K_j) is separable; choose a countable dense set 𝒟_j ⊆ C(K_j).

STEP 2 (bounds). M_j := sup_kμ_k(K_j) < ∞ by hypothesis. Each K_j is closed, hence Borel and μ_k-measurable. For g ∈ C(K_j) let F_{j,k}(g) := ∫_{K_j}g dμ_k (g is bounded and continuous on the measurable set K_j of finite μ_k-measure). F_{j,k} is linear, F_{j,k}(g) ≥ 0 for g ≥ 0, and |F_{j,k}(g)| ≤ M_j‖g‖_∞.

STEP 3 (test functions). Each f ∈ C_c(X) := C_c(X, ℝ) is μ_k-integrable (bounded, continuous, support compact of finite measure), and if spt f ⊆ K_j then ∫_Xf dμ_k = F_{j,k}(f|_{K_j}), because f = 0 off K_j.

STEP 4 (one subsequence for all test functions; printed “by the Alaoglu theorem … choosing the subsequences successively and taking a diagonal sequence”, in its sequential form). Enumerate the countable set of pairs (j, g) with j ≥ 1, g ∈ 𝒟_j as (j_1, g_1), (j_2, g_2), …. Each real sequence (F_{j_p,k}(g_p))_k is bounded by M_{j_p}‖g_p‖_∞. By Bolzano–Weierstrass choose successively infinite sets ℕ ⊇ N_1 ⊇ N_2 ⊇ ⋯ such that (F_{j_p,k}(g_p))_{k∈N_p} converges, and let φ(k) be the k-th element of N_k (in increasing order). Then φ is strictly increasing (the k-th element of N_{k+1} ⊆ N_k is at least the k-th element of N_k, and the (k+1)-th element of N_{k+1} is larger) and (φ(k))_{k≥p} is a sequence in N_p, so F_{j,φ(k)}(g) converges for every j and every g ∈ 𝒟_j. For arbitrary g ∈ C(K_j) and η > 0 choose g' ∈ 𝒟_j with ‖g − g'‖_∞ < η; then
  |F_{j,φ(k)}(g) − F_{j,φ(l)}(g)| ≤ 2M_jη + |F_{j,φ(k)}(g') − F_{j,φ(l)}(g')|,
so (F_{j,φ(k)}(g))_k is Cauchy and converges. Hence F_j(g) := lim_kF_{j,φ(k)}(g) exists for all j and all g ∈ C(K_j).

STEP 5 (the limit functional). For f ∈ C_c(X) choose j with spt f ⊆ K_j (Step 1). By Step 3, ∫_Xf dμ_{φ(k)} = F_{j,φ(k)}(f|_{K_j}) converges as k → ∞. Define F(f) := lim_k∫_Xf dμ_{φ(k)}; this is the limit of a real sequence that does not depend on j, so no compatibility between the F_j is needed. F is linear (limits of the linear maps f ↦ ∫f dμ_{φ(k)}) and positive (F(f) ≥ 0 if f ≥ 0, a limit of nonnegative numbers).

STEP 6 (Riesz; printed “by applying Theorem 4.12”). The restriction of F to K₊ = C_c(X, [0, ∞)) is additive, positively homogeneous and [0, ∞)-valued, i.e. an ℝ≥0-linear map C_c(X, ℝ≥0) → ℝ≥0. By Theorem 4.12 (sibling `riesz_positive`) there is a Radon outer measure μ on X with F(f) = ∫_Xf dμ for all f ∈ K₊. For f ∈ C_c(X) write f = f⁺ − f⁻ with f^± := max{±f, 0} ∈ K₊; by linearity F(f) = F(f⁺) − F(f⁻) = ∫f⁺ dμ − ∫f⁻ dμ = ∫_Xf dμ (f⁺, f⁻ are μ-integrable).

STEP 7 (conclusion). For every f ∈ C_c(X, ℝ), ∫_Xf dμ_{φ(k)} → F(f) = ∫_Xf dμ as k → ∞; φ is strictly increasing and μ is a Radon outer measure. ∎

Formalization note (non-binding): second countability gives σ-compactness and metrizability through Mathlib instances (`sigmaCompactSpace_of_locallyCompact_secondCountable`, `metrizableSpace_of_t3_secondCountable`), `CompactExhaustion.choice` gives the exhaustion with `exists_superset_of_isCompact`, and `ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace` gives separability of C(K_j). SimonGMT only has the compact metrizable case `simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable` (Chapter01/CompactMetrizableCompactness.lean), whose Prokhorov-based subsequence lemma `finiteMeasure_tendsto_subseq_of_compact_metrizable` can replace Step 4 on each K_j (with a diagonal argument), or one can extract a single subsequence in the first-countable compact space Π_j([0, M_j] × ProbabilityMeasure(Y_j)) with nonempty pieces Y_j := K_j ∪ {x₀} (X ≠ ∅; the case X = ∅ is trivial), normalizing a zero measure to a Dirac mass. Step 6 uses `Submission.riesz_positive`; integrals of continuous compactly supported functions against `caratheodoryMeasure` agree with those against the Borel restriction (`integral_trim`).
proof_key_steps: Erratum: assume second countability, so X is σ-compact and metrizable.
Exhaustion K_j ⊆ int K_{j+1}: every compact set lies in some K_j, and each C(K_j) is separable.
The functionals F_{j,k}(g) = ∫_{K_j} g dμ_k are bounded by M_j‖g‖_∞.
A diagonal subsequence φ along countable dense sets, extended to all of C(K_j) by the uniform bounds (sequential Alaoglu).
F(f) := lim_k ∫ f dμ_{φ(k)} for f ∈ C_c(X) is linear and positive.
Theorem 4.12 on C_c(X, ℝ≥0) gives a Radon μ; extend to signed f via f = f⁺ − f⁻.
